title: New Talent Tech Stack Playbook — First 90 / Role Enablement
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents the recommended toolchain, provisioning flow, access guardrails, and role-specific first-90-day enablement checklist for new hires at Redwood. It is intended for people-ops, hiring managers, and platform engineers who operate onboarding automation and access controls. The goal is to reduce time-to-productivity while keeping credentials, cost centers, and sensitive data secured.

Why this exists:
- New hires should have 80% of job-essential tooling ready within the first day and 95% by day 7.
- Reduce manual steps by centralizing patterns and automations.
- Provide consistent, auditable deprovisioning and role changes.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors (with >30 day contracts), and interns.
- Covers core SaaS and platform access: Identity (Okta), source control (GitHub), cloud (GCP projects), collaboration (Slack/Google Workspace), monitoring (Datadog), cost & billing (FinOps dashboard), Redwood Console and Dedicated admin consoles.

Tooling Inventory (primary systems):
1) Identity & SSO
   - Okta (primary IdP) — groups mapped to role templates.
   - 2FA enforced for all accounts; hardware token options for high privilege.
2) Source Control
   - GitHub org: team membership via SCIM provisioning + IaC team templates.
3) Cloud and Infra
   - GCP: project-level IAM roles, terraform-managed project bootstrap.
   - Dedicated GPU cluster admin consoles (Redwood-internal) — RBAC controlled.
4) Collaboration
   - Google Workspace: mail, calendar, Drive templates for onboarding.
   - Slack: channels auto-joined based on role metadata.
5) Observability & Deploy
   - Datadog: dashboard access read/write by role.
   - Redwood Console: product-level access for SRE, Platform, and Support.
6) Finance & Procurement
   - Internal FinOps dashboard (read for managers, cost-owner write).
7) Secrets & Keys
   - Vault (HashiCorp) or KMS for private deployments.

Role-Based Access Matrix (summary table):
| Role type            | GitHub | GCP (prod) | Datadog | Vault (secrets) | Redwood Console | Slack admin |
| -------------------- | ------ | ---------- | ------- | --------------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| IC Engineer (backend)| write  | dev*       | read    | no              | read            | no         |
| SRE / Platform       | write  | ops        | write   | limited         | admin           | yes        |
| Product / PM         | read   | none       | read    | no              | product-read    | no         |
| Sales / GTM          | read   | none       | none    | no              | account-read    | no         |
| Contractor (eng)     | write* | dev        | none    | no              | read            | no         |

*dev = development projects only; write* indicates branch-restricted PR flows enforced.

Provisioning SLAs and Targets:
- Day 0 (first 8 business hours): Okta account created, Google Workspace account provisioned, primary Slack account invited. Target: 95% completion.
- Day 1 (within 24 hours): GitHub team membership and basic repo access granted (private repos may take longer pending approvals). Target: 80% completion for role-critical repos.
- Day 3 (72 hours): Cloud dev project access, Datadog read access, Redwood Console read access.
- Day 7: Remaining access and whitelists completed (service accounts, billing mapping).
- Deprovisioning target: initiated within 2 hours of termination notification; full removal or suspension within 24 hours for contractors, 48 hours for employees pending HR completion.

Automated Provisioning Flow (high-level):
1) Offer accepted triggers: People-ops creates user stub in HRIS and flips hire flag.
2) CI job picks up HRIS event and calls onboarding-orchestrator via API.
   - Example: curl -X POST https://onboard.redwood.internal/api/v1/provision -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"hris_id":"12345","role":"backend_engineer","start_date":"2026-02-01"}'
3) Orchestrator actions (parallel where safe):
   - Create Okta user and assign role template.
   - Provision Google Workspace mailbox and Drive templates.
   - SCIM add to GitHub org teams.
   - Create Vault identity and set up least-privilege secret policies.
   - Create service account in GCP (dev) and add to terraform workspace.
4) Post-provision jobs: Slack invites, calendar onboarding event, send manager checklist email.

Manual/Approval Gates:
- Production GitHub write and GCP prod IAM require manager + security reviewer approval. Approval captured via PR in the "access-requests" repo; automation merges request after two approvers.
- Contractor elevated access must include sponsor and people-ops attestation.

First-90 Role Enablement Checklist (by day):
Day 0 (before first day or on arrival):
- HRIS and Okta account active; 2FA configured.
- Welcome email with slate of links: handbook, benefit portal, team README.
- Manager assigns onboarding buddy and first-week goal.

Day 1–7:
- Complete security baseline training and pass short quiz (SLO: complete by day 3).
- Access to dev repos and dev GCP projects; run first local build.
- Account for cost center in FinOps dashboard.

Day 8–30:
- Shadow deploy with mentor; run through rollback & incident responder playbook.
- Completed role-specific learning paths in LXP (Learning Experience Platform).
- Confirm Datadog alert visibility and runbook links are accessible.

Day 31–90:
- Contributor to a minor PR or customer-facing task.
- Performance review checkpoint with manager and people-ops.
- Confirm retention of all required credentials and completion of compliance items (SOC2/ISO modules as applicable).

Onboarding Automation Runbook (for SRE / Platform engineers):
1) When a new provisioning failure alert fires (tag: onboarding-orchestrator, severity=high):
   a) Check logs: kubectl -n onboarding logs deploy/orchestrator --tail=200
   b) Check service health: curl -sS https://onboard.health | jq .status
   c) If Okta provisioning is failing: check Okta API rate limits and tokens (owner: Jordan Kim).
2) Escalation path:
   - Triage on-call -> Platform lead (Marco Ruiz) -> People-ops lead (Priya Nair) for HR/contract issues.
3) Recovery steps:
   - Retry job after token refresh.
   - Manually trigger scoped provisioning for impacted user(s) via admin console endpoints.

Deprovision Checklist (termination & role changes):
- Step 1: HR closes employment in HRIS and sets termination timestamp.
- Step 2: Orchestrator suspends Okta account (immediate).
- Step 3: Revoke cloud keys and rotate any shared service-account keys the user had access to.
- Step 4: Remove GitHub membership and reassign code ownership where open PRs exist.
- Step 5: Revoke Vault access and rotate secrets if secret privileged access existed.
- Step 6: People-ops creates offboarding checklist for exit interviews, equipment return, and benefits.

Cost Controls and Billing Mapping:
- Every new hire must be assigned a cost center tag in payroll and GCP resource labels.
- Managers receive weekly reports if new hire resource spend exceeds $200 in the first 30 days.

Ownership and Metrics (who measures success):
- People-ops: % of hires meeting Day 0 and Day 7 SLA, onboarding satisfaction (survey NPS).
- Platform: automation success rate, mean-time-to-provision (MTTP).
- Security: compliance completion rate for baseline trainings and high-privileged approvals.

Common Questions / FAQ:
Q: Who to contact if Slack invite never arrives?
A: Email people-ops@redwood.com and ping #platform-oncall. That channel has an onboarding bot that can re-send invites.

Q: I need temporary prod access for debugging — what is the fastest route?
A: Submit an access-request PR in the access-requests repo. Include reason, duration (max 72 hours), and your manager as approver. Security will expedite critical ops requests.

Q: How are contractors handled differently?
A: Contractors get time-bound accounts and elevated access requires a sponsor and people-ops sign-off. Contractors are deprovisioned within 24 hours of end date.

Appendix A — Example role template (Okta group metadata):
{
  "group_name": "eng-backend-new-hire",
  "members": ["okta:uid:..."],
  "provisioning": {
    "github_team": "eng-backend",
    "gcp_projects": ["dev-backend-123"],
    "slack_channels": ["#eng-backend", "#onboarding"]
  }
}

Appendix B — Quick checklist for hiring managers (one-pager):
1) Verify offer details in HRIS before start.
2) Confirm cost center and code owner.
3) Assign buddy and create first-week plan in the team README.
4) Run through security & compliance checklist with new hire before granting prod access.

Document review cadence:
- People-ops will review and update this playbook every 6 months or when a major tool changes (Okta/SCIM/GitHub SSO), whichever comes first.
